summary: Re-review of revised state-model.json against the prior verdict (state-model-review.json @ revise). All five critical issues (CI-1..CI-5) and all six important improvements (II-1..II-6), plus both missing-items (MI-1, MI-2) and both unsafe-assumptions (UA-1, UA-2) are addressed with substantive, code-grounded revisions. Spot-checks of the new citations confirm: (a) lib/inventory/kernel/operations/manufacturing.ts:381-426 does write inventoryEvents with eventType='manufacturing_ingredient_consumption' on pick (verified — `consumeLotAllocationsForDemandInTx` and `consumeStockFifoInTx` both pass eventType='manufacturing_ingredient_consumption'), which makes T13b_unreachable correct and T13a's batch-mode-only reachability constraint accurate; (b) lib/db/schema/inventory-idempotency.ts:29-32 has the unique index on (organizationId, idempotencyKey) exactly as cited, supporting T02/T23/T27's ledger-row-count observable; (c) app/api/sales-orders/bulk-confirm/route.ts:12 calls requireIdempotencyKey('bulkConfirmSalesOrders'), and bulkConfirmSalesOrders DAL at sales/queries.ts:7597-7623 wraps payload in beginInventoryOperationInTx with the replay branch at 7609-7611 — T27 is faithful; (d) deleteManufacturingOrdersInTx at queries.ts:6379-6500 has the exact four-tier finalized guard the model describes (status/completedAt/actualQuantity at 6379-6391, completed-batch at 6393-6420, ingredient.actualQuantity at 6422-6444, consumption-event at 6446-6500) — T13a's guards and T13b_unreachable's failure_mode citations are line-accurate; (e) FOR UPDATE at manufacturing/queries.ts:3674 and the refresh-conflict guard at 3720-3752 are present exactly as cited, supporting T05's anti-duplication observable. The T13a/T13b split correctly resolves the prior reachability paradox: startBatch (T10) advances `manufacturingOrderBatches.status` from 'pending' to 'in_progress' WITHOUT writing consumption events, so a batch-started-but-not-picked MO can still be cancelled; pickIngredient (T09) writes consumption events synchronously, so a pick-induced MO_WORK_STARTED MO cannot be cancelled (T13b_unreachable). Confirmed by reading lib/inventory/kernel/operations/manufacturing.ts:381-426. T18b and T19b are reachable through the state graph (CLAIM_STALE_SNAPSHOT is entered via T16 or T21, and the new transitions provide the missing outbound edges). T27 (bulkConfirmSalesOrders) is fully grounded in code and schema. T24's demotion to 'MO_ACTIVE (outcome experimentally unknown)' is an acceptable hedge — the model commits enough for downstream test generation (predicts two rows, cites the absence of all four guard layers: route Idempotency-Key, DAL replay wrap, validateSalesLineLinkInTx existing_active_mo check, and DB unique constraint on salesOrderLineId) while flagging Phase 4 must run the empirical POST-twice test to confirm. The only minor residual: T24's observable_changes still asserts 'two MO rows result' as the expected outcome, which is slightly more committal than the to_state's 'experimentally unknown' phrasing, but the failure_mode block explicitly covers the alternative branch, so downstream test design can handle both outcomes. Overall verdict: pass. All scores >= 5.

Code verification I performed directly: lib/inventory/kernel/operations/manufacturing.ts:381-426 writes inventoryEvents with eventType='manufacturing_ingredient_consumption' on every pick via both consumeLotAllocationsForDemandInTx (heldConsumed) at lines 381-395 and consumeStockFifoInTx (fifoConsumed) at lines 405-426. Confirmed eventType='manufacturing_ingredient_consumption' on lines 388 and 412. This means: (a) T09's observable is correct (pick DOES write consumption events), (b) T13b_unreachable is correct (pick-induced MO_WORK_STARTED is permanently uncancellable via DELETE because the 6446-6500 guard fires), (c) T13a's preconditions correctly require batch-mode entry via startBatch (T10 cite at state-model.json:865 explicitly notes 'No manufacturing_ingredient_consumption events written at this point').
